title: Undated respiratory practical answer-key paper
note: Twenty original MCQs, including a shared spirogram and sixteen image spotters. Posting date 4 September 2025 is not an exam date. Yellow highlights are supplied answers and were audited separately.

questions.prompt: A 25-year-old man, height 175 cm, has the shown spirogram; temperature coefficient = 1.1. Which one is the following patient’s Tidal Volume?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Disputed: the source highlights A (330 mL), but the displayed tidal swings run from 1000 to 1400 mL. Applying the stated 1.1 correction gives 440 mL, which is absent from the options. Do not score.

media.alt: Original spirogram with volume scale and time calibration.

questions.prompt: A 25-year-old man, height 175 cm, has the shown spirogram; temperature coefficient = 1.1. What is his Vital Capacity (VC)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: The displayed maximal volume change is 3000 mL; multiplying by 1.1 gives 3300 mL.

media.alt: Original spirogram with volume scale and time calibration.

questions.prompt: Which internal factors play a role in determining a person’s Predicted Vital Capacity (PVC)?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: Age, height and sex are inputs to predicted spirometric values.

questions.prompt: What is the normal value for ratio of FEV1/FVC?
questions.subject: physiology
questions.note: D is the conventional young-adult teaching answer. Clinical interpretation uses age-appropriate reference values and lower limits of normal rather than a universal 80% diagnostic threshold.

questions.prompt: What is the name of cell shown by arrow?
questions.subject: histology
questions.note: Unresolved: the source highlights 'Pneumococcus Type III', a nonstandard answer for alveolar epithelial identification. 'Pneumococcus' appears to be a repeated printing error for pneumocyte; no Type III pneumocyte option can be validated from this figure. Preserve the image and supplied key without scoring.
